analysis:
The PR is documentation-only: docs/developer/desktop-app.md (date bump plus the Autopilot recommendation paragraph at head lines 416-425) and docs/reference/desktop-control.md (date bump and the /control/v1/network row at line 70). No code, keys, attestation, authorization, encryption or cache-storage behavior changes, so no canonical threat (T-041, TB-002, TB-007, TB-011 and similar) is weakened.

The base text excerpt at lines 487-634 shows the same content as the head at 494-641, shifted by 7 lines. This is consistent with the seven-line insertion at head 416-425 and nothing else.

The doc describes the renderer ranking models by per-chip earnings (`by_chip`, `by_chip_window: "24h"`) taken from public, unauthenticated /v1/stats data relayed unchanged through the local native API. The data is consumer-visible aggregate network information and not a sensitive asset. It can influence which models the user is recommended and whether they are downloaded or enrolled. Recommendations are advisory: the user checks the models, Swift re-verifies the downloaded inventory and pin capacity, and the coordinator still decides admission.

An adversarial or compromised stats source could skew recommendations, but that trust relationship exists already (seven-day model_earnings) and the PR adds no new trust boundary. The doc describes a fallback to seven-day totals when per-chip rows recommend no servable model. The implementation (recommendations.ts, the relay in DesktopBackend.resource) is not supplied. A next pass should check that the relay applies bounds and validation to the unchanged `by_chip` payload and that the renderer treats the values as untrusted numbers. This is an unverified contract, not a finding.

No security regression is identified in the supplied docs.
